analysis.title: "Blast Radius": These Are The AI Junk Bonds Set To Crater As Democrats Freeze The Buildout
key_insights: Of 20 data center bonds in the junk market, only one has Morgan Stanley's preferred protection requiring rent commencement once shells are delivered regardless of power availability. The article ranks all 20 by exposure to the Nov 3 Democratic election wins.
Seven bonds worth $17.3B score in the article's 'danger zone'. The market has marked them down about 5 points on average since late September, nearly four times as much as the rest.
The universe is $45.6B of debt financing 4,063MW of critical IT capacity. Only 468MW has been delivered, 2,512MW is due between now and end-2027 and 744MW in 2028.
Goldman estimates Democratic state-level wins could lead to moratoria affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas alone at roughly a quarter.

Ten bonds (nine sited entirely in states that flipped to a Democratic governor, plus Core Scientific's CORZ spread across four states) account for about $24.3B, or 53% of the universe, and 2.1GW of 4.1GW.
$17.5B of bonds in newly blue states back projects not scheduled to finish until after the Texas legislature adjourns May 31, 2027: Galaxy, both Tracts, Clearspark and CORZ.

Per Jefferies, Governor-elect Hinojosa's proposed pause targets new permits and grid approvals and spares projects already under construction. The article says the realistic risk for most bonds is delay, repricing and re-litigation more than an outright halt. The platform also makes large loads pay for generation and interconnection, phases out data center tax exemptions worth at least $1B a year, and freezes residential rates.

Barclays says permitting risk had been viewed as 'more bark than bite' until this week. By its count only 2 of 27 IG and HY data center bonds are fully operational and only 4 have date-certain rent. In junk those are APLD (operational) and SECMOS (date-certain rent).

Galaxy Helios (GALAXY 9.875% '31, $3.51B) is a 260MW CoreWeave campus in Lubbock, due March 2028. It traded at 97 on Sep 28 and closed at 90.75 (12.5% yield). Per MS Exhibit 62 it trades only about 200bp inside CoreWeave unsecured paper vs about 380bp for the operational APLD bonds, so the market gives the collateral little credit.

Tract twins (TRACTC 5.875% '31, TRACTD 6.5% '31, $8.39B combined) are 400MW in Storey County, Nevada with NVIDIA as tenant, delivering April and June 2028. TRACTC is down another 3.5 points to 87.8 and TRACTD down 2.4 to 89.7. MS flagged that the TRACT/NVDA relationship is an exception, with TRACTC about 290bp behind NVIDIA bonds.

Zenith Arc (ZENARC 8.875% '31, $2.25B) is the cheapest bond at 84.25 (13.4%), down 7.5 points since Sep 28, with Jane Street as tenant and 149MW due October 2028. Oklahoma did not flip, so it shows the market charges for construction duration regardless of politics.
Edged Compute (EDGCOM 7.5% '31, $1.30B, CoreWeave/Alibaba, Chicago and Atlanta, due Dec 2027) is down 7 points to 85.25. MS already had it at a 16% yield-to-call.

Virginia pair: DDRIVE 8.875% '31 (DDC Richmond, 76MW, CoreWeave) fell from about 98 to 92.1 in six weeks. YNDRDC 6.875% '31 (Yondr, Loudoun, Oracle tenant, due Oct 2028) trades about 220bp behind Oracle bonds vs about 185bp for North Dakota-sited PFORGE with the same tenant. Virginia moratorium bills are advancing before the Jan 13 session.
Core Scientific CORZ 7.75% '31 ($3.30B, 590MW across TX, GA, OK, NC, final delivery June 30, 2027) is down 5 points to 92.1.

Bonds with existing buildings (APLD, WULF, FLASHC) or an IG tenant with near-term delivery (Amazon's Black Pearl, Meta's Clearspark, Google-backstopped Cipher) are within a point or two of September levels.

Refinancing is a second risk. Most bonds are callable 2027-2028 and mature 2030-2031, sized on budgets set before 'chipflation'. MS's Shawn Kim says AI/cloud buyers lock in chip supply first while non-LTA buyers compete for a smaller residual pool. CoreWeave is the tenant on seven of the 20 bonds.

With the 5-year near 4.75%, CoreWeave's four unsecured notes (15.4-15.9%) are above the 1,000bp distressed threshold. Galaxy is about 775bp over, Zenith about 865bp and Edged about 710bp, so 135-290bp from that threshold.

MS (Oct 1) preferred collateral-backed over unsecured risk and argued that energized megawatts gain scarcity value. Barclays agrees that DCs with power gain a scarcity advantage. The article argues the same scarcity lowers the value of everything still in the pipeline, which is about three-quarters of junk capacity.
Goldman credit strategists think post-election widening makes AI credit 'more attractive'. The article agrees for hyperscaler bonds but sides with the TRACE tape on half-built shells.

market_movers.rationale: Tenant on seven of the 20 junk data center bonds. Its unsecured notes trade at 78.5-83 cents (about 15.5% YTM) and a CoreWeave stumble is named as a trigger for distress in the project bonds.
CORZ 7.75% '31 ($3.30B, 590MW across TX, GA, OK, NC) is down 5 points to 92.1, with final delivery a month after the Texas session ends.
Operational with date-certain rent, so its bonds are insulated. They trade about 380bp inside CoreWeave unsecured paper.

sector_views.rationale: Pipeline developers carry permit delay, cost and refinancing risk after Democratic governor wins in TX, GA and NV. Operational or IG-tenant bonds are holding up.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Used as the base for the 1,000bp distressed-spread threshold. CoreWeave's unsecured notes at 15.4-15.9% are already past it.

risk_factors: Permitting and moratorium risk in newly Democratic states, including a Texas freeze running into summer, a Georgia pause or a Nevada rewrite of large-load tariffs.
CoreWeave counterparty and funding stress as tenant on seven of the 20 bonds.
Chip supply and cost inflation ('chipflation') hitting non-LTA neocloud buyers.
Refinancing risk with callability in 2027-2028 and maturities in 2030-2031.
Higher project costs from large-load tariffs, loss of data center tax exemptions worth at least $1B a year, and residential rate freezes.
Rate sensitivity of project-level financing, per Morgan Stanley.
geopolitical: Nov 3 US state elections: Democratic governors won in Texas, Georgia and Nevada, with a Democratic PSC majority in Georgia and Ohio also named as flipping.
Texas 90th Legislature runs to May 31, 2027, and Governor Abbott's audit-driven pause becomes legislation-based.
Virginia data center moratorium bills are advancing ahead of the Jan 13 session.

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley preferred collateral-backed risk, with scarcity value for powered data centers. Goldman credit strategists say the post-election widening makes AI credit more attractive. Operational and IG-tenant bonds are within a point or two of September levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Pipeline bonds back unpowered shells with delivery dates after the Texas session ends, face permit delay, tariff and tax changes, chip cost inflation and refinancing risk. About three-quarters of junk capacity is still in the pipeline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Texas freeze running into summer, a Georgia pause, a Nevada rewrite of large-load tariffs or a CoreWeave stumble would each push the worst project bonds toward the 1,000bp distressed spread.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pipeline bonds will most likely be priced on the date the power gets turned on, and nobody can say when that is.
